title: Streamline span propagation and compact log encoder to cut trace overhead
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Our runtime shows a measurable per-request CPU and allocation overhead from the current tracing glue (OpenTelemetry SDK + custom adapters) and the log encoder we use to attach trace context to structured logs. This ticket removes excess allocations in span propagation, replaces the current reflection-based log encoder with a compact encoder, and consolidates the tracing hook points to reduce duplicate work.

Goals:
- Reduce median CPU per-request overhead from tracing by ~25% on p50 workload.
- Cut per-request allocations attributable to telemetry by >=40%.
- Maintain parity for spans emitted (trace IDs, attributes) and sampling semantics.
- Ship with safe, gradual rollout and metrics to detect regressions.

Approach:
1) Replace the context carrier layer with a zero-copy context-carrier that stores only the minimal keys we need for routing and sampling decisions. This eliminates two allocation-heavy map clones per request.
2) Unify tracing hook entry points: move route-level, model-run, and batch-worker hooks behind a single lightweight pre-span-check to avoid emitting duplicate attributes and to short-circuit when tracing is disabled.
3) Swap the runtime's reflection-based log encoder for a compact, allocation-minimizing encoder (based on flatbuffers-lite style buffer writes) that writes trace fields inline into the log buffer.
4) Add an opt-in compatibility shim for downstream consumers during rollout (runtime config flag: telemetry.legacy_context).

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated perf harness shows >=25% CPU reduction on p50 and >=40% allocation reduction for telemetry path (before -> after).
- End-to-end traces remain compatible with current sampling policy and show no missing essential attributes for the top 10 instrumented endpoints.
- No high-severity errors or increased error-rate observed in canary for 48 hours.
- All new code has unit tests and integration acceptance tests in CI.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting full OpenTelemetry SDKs. We will keep using the upstream SDK but reduce our glue-code cost.

Stakeholders: runtime team (owner), telemetry team (review), platform infra (release), QA, product (for customer impact assessment).
progress_updates: 2025-02-06: Spike completed — microbenchmark shows ~18% CPU advantage from zero-copy carrier on a synthetic request generator.
2025-02-10: Design review with telemetry team; agreed on carrier API and compatibility shim semantics. Action: telemetry to review proto on 2025-02-12.
2025-02-13: First draft patch implements unified hook and zero-copy carrier. Benchmarks: allocation down ~35%, CPU down ~22% on p50. Not yet meeting CPU target; next step is log encoder replacement.
2025-02-18: Compact log encoder PoC merged to feature branch; local load test shows additional 10% CPU reduction when combined with carrier changes. Preparing PR and expanded perf runs.
2025-02-20: Integration tests added; starting a 48h canary on staging-runtime-3. Canary config: telemetry.legacy_context=false for 10% traffic, true for remaining.

testing_plan: Unit tests for carrier and encoder with edge-case context keys and large attribute sets.
Integration test: end-to-end trace emit to Jaeger/OTLP collector and attribute verification.
Perf harness run: synthetic p50/p95 CPU & allocations with real request payloads (100k requests).
Canary: staged routing 10% no-legacy, 90% legacy for 48h then ramp down if stable.
rollout_plan: Feature flag guarded rollout: feature off by default. Step 1: internal staging canary 10% traffic for 48h. Step 2: increase to 50% for 24h if no regressions. Step 3: full rollout and disable compatibility shim after 2 weeks if no issues.
observability_changes: New metric: telemetry.carrier.alloc_bytes (gauge) — measure allocations attributable to carrier operations.
New metric: telemetry.encoder.encode_ns (histogram) — encode time distribution.
Tracing: preserve trace_id/span_id and sampling decision; add attribute telemetry.carrier.version for rollbacks.
Alert: telemetry.encoder.error_rate > 0.1% over 1h => rollback automation trigger.
